paper.title: Adversarial Resilience of Poisson-Process Submodular Maximization over Matroids, and Full-Bandit Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Nonnegative submodular maximization over a matroid with a xi-controlled (adversarially perturbed, persistent) value oracle
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline approximation algorithm for submodular maximization under a perturbed value oracle; not a bandit problem.
unmapped: value oracle error |f_hat(S)-f(S)| <= xi for all S, known radius xi
matroid constraint of rank k with independence oracle
objective f:2^U->[0,1] nonnegative submodular, possibly non-monotone
guarantee is an approximation ratio relative to OPT
settings.definition_quote: A $\xierr$-controlled oracle is a function $\widehat f:2^U\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $|\widehat f(S)-f(S)|\le\xierr$ for all $S\subseteq U$. The perturbation is deterministic and may be adversarial; no stochastic or independence assumption is imposed.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic full-bandit CMAB with general matroid constraint and submodular mean reward
unmapped: actions are independent sets of a rank-k matroid on n base elements
mean reward f(S) is nonnegative submodular (monotone or non-monotone); realized rewards need not be submodular
exploration may play sets in I^{+1} (independent after deleting at most one element); exploitation and benchmark in I
settings.definition_quote: at round $t$ the learner chooses an admissible super-arm $A_t$ and observes only an aggregate reward $Y_t\in[0,1]$. Each play of $S$ supplies an independent draw from a fixed distribution of mean $f(S)$ ... $R_\alpha(T):=\alpha T\OPT-\mathbb E\left[\sum_{t=1}^T Y_t\right]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic full-bandit CMAB with unit-capacity partition matroid and submodular mean reward
unmapped: unit-capacity partition matroid with k parts on n elements
exploration may play sets in I^{+1}
settings.definition_quote: Throughout this section $M=(U,\I)$ is a partition matroid of rank $k$: the ground set $U$ is partitioned into $P_1,\ldots,P_k$ and $S\in\I$ iff $|S\cap P_j|\le1$ for every $j$.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For every $\eps\in(0,1/2]$, supplied error bound $\xierr\ge0$, and persistent $\xierr$-controlled oracle, the truncated SGS-Poisson value-oracle implementation ... outputs $A_{\rm out}\in\I$ satisfying $\E[f(A_{\rm out})]\ge (1/e-\eps)\OPT-Ck\xierr$ (non-monotone) ... with $C=8$, and makes at most $N(\eps)=O(nk\log\frac1\eps+\frac{nk^2\log n\log(1/\eps)}{\eps^2}+\frac{nk\log^2(1/\eps)}{\eps^2})$ oracle calls, deterministically.

results.notes: Lower bound on expected value of output (approximation guarantee), recorded as 'other'. Oracle complexity O(nk^2 log n eps^-2 log^2(1/eps)) deterministic. Theorem 7.4 gives the same guarantee for unit-capacity partition matroids with O(nk log n eps^-2 log^2(1/eps)) calls.

source.label: cor:cmab
source.quote: Consider stochastic full-bandit CMAB with $n\ge2$, a general rank-$k$ matroid with $k\ge1$, a nonnegative submodular mean reward, and Assumption~\ref{ass:action-set}. Let $\psi=O(nk^2\log n)$ and $\delta=8k$. Then for every horizon $T\ge\max\{2,\psi\}$ there exist algorithms with $R_{1/e}(T)=\widetilde O(n^{1/5}k^{4/5}T^{4/5})$ (non-monotone), $R_{1-1/e}(T)=\widetilde O(n^{1/5}k^{4/5}T^{4/5})$ (monotone).

results.notes: 1/e-regret: alpha*T*OPT - E[sum Y_t]; recorded as quantity 'other' since it is an alpha-regret. Anytime version via doubling (Remark 3.5) up to log factors.

source.label: thm:partition
source.quote: Hence the implementation is $(1/e,2,2,\psi,8k)$- and $(1-1/e,2,2,\psi,8k)$-resilient with $\psi=O(nk\log n)$, and under Assumption~\ref{ass:action-set}, for $T\ge\max\{2,\psi\}$, $R_{1/e}(T)=\widetilde O(n^{1/5}k^{3/5}T^{4/5})$, $R_{1-1/e}(T)=\widetilde O(n^{1/5}k^{3/5}T^{4/5})$, respectively for non-monotone and monotone objectives.

results.notes: 1/e-regret recorded as 'other'. Theorem also restates offline guarantee of Theorem 5.14 with oracle budget O(nk log(1/eps) + nk log n log(1/eps)/eps^2 + n log^2(1/eps)/eps^2).
